_meta.source: Compiled from public agricultural extension service guidelines (ICAR, TNAU, KVK, USDA-ARS)
_meta.disclaimer: These are clinical reference guidelines. Follow local agricultural extension rules and product label instructions for exact pesticide rates.

severity_guidance.LOW: Remove and destroy fallen leaves. Prune canopy to promote rapid drying. Monitor new leaves weekly.
severity_guidance.MEDIUM: Apply protectant fungicide: Mancozeb 75 WP @ 2.5g/L or Captan 50 WP @ 2g/L at 10-14 day intervals during wet periods.
severity_guidance.HIGH: Apply systemic curative fungicide: Difenoconazole 25 EC @ 0.5ml/L or Myclobutanil 10 WP @ 0.5g/L. Remove severely infected twigs and fruit.

cultural_practices: Rake and destroy fallen leaves in autumn or apply 5% urea spray to speed leaf decomposition
Prune trees annually to maintain open center canopy for maximum sun and airflow
Plant scab-resistant cultivars (e.g., Liberty, Prima, Enterprise) in new plantings
Avoid overhead irrigation; use drip or under-tree micro-sprinklers
Apple___Apple_scab.monitoring_note: Re-scan new terminal leaves after 7 days to verify no olive-green fungal lesions appear.

severity_guidance.LOW: Prune out dead shoots and mummified fruits. Disinfect shears with 70% ethanol between cuts.
severity_guidance.MEDIUM: Apply Captan 50 WP @ 2.5g/L or Thiophanate-methyl 70 WP @ 1g/L every 10 to 14 days from petal fall.
severity_guidance.HIGH: Aggressively cut back cankered limbs at least 15 cm below infected tissue. Burn infected wood immediately. Apply protective copper fungicide.

cultural_practices: Remove all mummified apples hanging on trees or lying on ground before winter
Prune dead twigs, fire blight strikes, and winter-injured wood which harbor fungal spores
Prevent mechanical bark injury and insect damage that provide fungal entry sites
Apple___Black_rot.monitoring_note: Inspect branch bark and fruit clusters for black pycnidia pustules after 10 days.

severity_guidance.LOW: Inspect nearby Juniper/Cedar trees. Prune out cedar rust galls within 500m radius if feasible.
severity_guidance.MEDIUM: Spray Myclobutanil 10 WP @ 0.5g/L or Mancozeb 75 WP @ 2g/L at pink bud through petal fall.
severity_guidance.HIGH: Apply sterol inhibitor fungicide (Difenoconazole 25 EC @ 0.5ml/L) immediately to stop aecia spore formation. Repeat in 10 days.

cultural_practices: Remove red cedar and ornamental juniper hosts near the orchard boundary
Plant rust-resistant apple varieties (e.g., Freedom, Liberty, Redfree)
Schedule preventive sprays during spring rainy spells when galls produce spore horns
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.monitoring_note: Check upper leaf surfaces for bright yellow-orange spots with dark dots.

severity_guidance.LOW: Canopy is vigorous and disease-free. Maintain routine balanced nutrition and orchard sanitation.
severity_guidance.MEDIUM: Optimal health. Continue preventive dormant oil and copper sanitation spray schedule.
severity_guidance.HIGH: Excellent condition. Maintain regular scouting during rainy vegetative flushes.

cultural_practices: Maintain clean tree basins free of weed competition
Apply balanced NPK with micronutrients (Boron, Zinc) based on annual soil analysis
Ensure adequate mulch and regulated irrigation during fruit sizing
Apple___healthy.monitoring_note: Routine scouting in 3 weeks or after significant rain events.

severity_guidance.LOW: Foliage is green and healthy. Maintain soil acidity (pH 4.5-5.2) and organic mulch depth.
severity_guidance.MEDIUM: Healthy. Continue regular acid-loving fertilization (ammonium sulfate).
severity_guidance.HIGH: Vigorous growth. Monitor drip lines for uniform moisture distribution.

cultural_practices: Maintain 8-10 cm pine bark or acidic organic mulch around root zones
Keep soil pH strictly between 4.5 and 5.5 using elemental sulfur if necessary
Irrigate with clean, low-salinity water to avoid iron chlorosis
Blueberry___healthy.monitoring_note: Regular inspection in 3 weeks to ensure no cane blight or leaf scorch.

severity_guidance.LOW: Prune out water sprouts and lower dense foliage to enhance sun penetration and air circulation.
severity_guidance.MEDIUM: Apply Wettable Sulfur 80 WP @ 3g/L or Potassium bicarbonate 5g/L early morning at first appearance.
severity_guidance.HIGH: Apply systemic fungicide: Trifloxystrobin + Tebuconazole @ 0.75ml/L or Myclobutanil @ 0.5ml/L. Repeat in 10 days.

cultural_practices: Avoid overhead irrigation; keep foliage dry particularly during evenings
Avoid excess nitrogen fertilization which triggers succulent susceptible growth flushes
Prune for open canopy to maximize interior tree sunlight exposure
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.monitoring_note: Check younger shoots and leaf undersides for powdery white mycelial coating.

severity_guidance.LOW: Leaves show vibrant deep green without spot or mildew signs. Maintain regular orchard care.
severity_guidance.MEDIUM: Vigorous tree. Ensure balanced post-harvest nutrition and trunk borer protection.
severity_guidance.HIGH: Excellent tree health. Maintain good orchard floor management.

cultural_practices: Ensure proper drip irrigation during fruit set and development
Sanitize dropped fruit and dead twigs to prevent monilinia brown rot buildup
Monitor orchard boundaries for aphid and fruit fly vectors

severity_guidance.LOW: Monitor lesions on lower leaves before tasseling. Lesions are rectangular and vein-bounded.
severity_guidance.MEDIUM: Apply foliar fungicide: Azoxystrobin 18.2% + Difenoconazole 11.4% SC @ 1ml/L at early silking stage.
severity_guidance.HIGH: Apply Pyraclostrobin + Fluxapyroxad @ 1ml/L. If disease reaches ear leaf prior to dough stage, spray immediately.

cultural_practices: Rotate fields away from corn for at least 1-2 seasons to break residue-borne inoculum
Deep till crop residue into soil after harvest to accelerate decomposition of fungal stroma
Plant high-yielding resistant or tolerant hybrid varieties suited to your agro-zone
Maintain balanced potassium nutrition to strengthen stalk and leaf cuticle
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.monitoring_note: Check ear leaf and leaves above ear for expansion of rectangular gray lesions.

severity_guidance.LOW: Few cinnamon-brown pustules on lower leaves; usually economic threshold not reached. Monitor weekly.
severity_guidance.MEDIUM: Apply Mancozeb 75 WP @ 2.5g/L or Propiconazole 25 EC @ 1ml/L if pustules spread before tasseling.
severity_guidance.HIGH: Apply Azoxystrobin + Propiconazole combination @ 1ml/L. Ensure full coverage on upper canopy.

cultural_practices: Select hybrids with Rp gene-mediated resistance to Puccinia sorghi
Plant early in the season to evade peak rust spore showers carried by southern winds
Avoid excessive nitrogen applications that delay crop maturity and increase susceptibility
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.monitoring_note: Re-scan upper canopy leaves for powdery cinnamon-brown pustules on both leaf surfaces.

severity_guidance.LOW: Monitor long cigar-shaped grayish-green lesions on bottom leaves. Disease favored by humid 18-27°C weather.
severity_guidance.MEDIUM: Apply Mancozeb 75 WP @ 2.5g/L or Tebuconazole 250 EC @ 1ml/L if lesions appear 2 weeks before silking.
severity_guidance.HIGH: Apply Strobilurin + Triazole combination (e.g. Azoxystrobin 200 g/l + Cyproconazole 80 g/l) @ 1ml/L.

cultural_practices: Use multi-race resistant corn hybrids with Ht gene resistance
Rotate with non-host crops like soybean, peanut, or sunflower for at least 1 year
Plow under corn stubble post-harvest to reduce overwintering conidia survival
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.monitoring_note: Check for development of olive-black fungal spores inside the cigar-shaped lesions.

severity_guidance.LOW: Crop shows vigorous dark green vegetative growth without leaf lesions or blight streaks.
severity_guidance.MEDIUM: Excellent vegetative stand. Ensure critical moisture during tasseling and silking stages.
severity_guidance.HIGH: Optimal crop condition. Maintain balanced topdressing with urea and zinc sulfate.

cultural_practices: Maintain weed-free conditions during early 30-45 days crop vegetative stage
Apply split nitrogen doses (basal, knee-high, and tasseling stages)
Scout for Fall Armyworm (Spodoptera frugiperda) whorl damage regularly
Corn_(maize)___healthy.monitoring_note: Inspect during tasseling stage for any sudden rust or blight development.

severity_guidance.LOW: Remove dried mummified berries from vines. Prune lower shoots for air circulation.
severity_guidance.MEDIUM: Apply Mancozeb 75 WP @ 2.5g/L or Captan 50 WP @ 2g/L before and immediately after bloom.
severity_guidance.HIGH: Apply Myclobutanil 10 WP @ 0.5g/L or Kresoxim-methyl 44.3 SC @ 0.6ml/L. Remove all infected clusters.

cultural_practices: Thoroughly collect and destroy all mummified berries from vine cordons and trellis floor
Canopy management: Shoot thinning, leaf pulling around fruiting zones to improve spray coverage
Mow vineyard ground cover to reduce relative humidity inside vine microclimate
Grape___Black_rot.monitoring_note: Inspect young berry clusters and young leaves for circular brown spots with dark margins.

severity_guidance.LOW: Tag symptomatic vines displaying tiger-stripe leaf interveinal chlorosis. Prune tagged vines last.
severity_guidance.MEDIUM: Disinfect all pruning cuts immediately with wound sealant containing copper or pyraclostrobin.
severity_guidance.HIGH: Trunk surgery: cut trunk below fungal white-rot spongy wood. If systemic, uproot and burn vine.

cultural_practices: Delay annual pruning until late winter when vine wound healing is faster and spore release is minimal
Never prune vines during rain or high humidity events
Sterilize pruning shears between vines with 70% alcohol or 10% sodium hypochlorite solution
Paint all large cuts (>2 cm diameter) with antifungal protective paste
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).monitoring_note: Monitor foliage for tiger-stripe pattern and berries for small dark measles spots.

severity_guidance.LOW: Remove early infected leaves showing brown angular spots. Increase canopy air movement.
severity_guidance.MEDIUM: Spray Mancozeb 75 WP @ 2.5g/L or Copper Oxychloride 50 WP @ 3g/L. Repeat in 10-12 days.
severity_guidance.HIGH: Apply Difenoconazole 25 EC @ 0.5ml/L or Azoxystrobin 23 SC @ 1ml/L. Ensure both leaf surfaces are wetted.

cultural_practices: Prune to eliminate canopy overcrowding and ensure rapid drying of dew on leaves
Collect fallen diseased leaves and burn or bury in deep trenches
Avoid excessive vegetative vigor through controlled nitrogen fertilization
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.monitoring_note: Re-scan leaf undersides for dark brown to black velvety fungal spore tufts.

severity_guidance.LOW: Vine foliage is clean, vigorous, and free from spots, mildew, or chlorosis.
severity_guidance.MEDIUM: Excellent canopy health. Maintain trellis positioning and shoot tucking.
severity_guidance.HIGH: Healthy vines. Maintain regulated deficit irrigation (RDI) for wine or table grape quality.

cultural_practices: Regular shoot positioning, leaf removal around clusters, and canopy management
Maintain balanced potassium and magnesium nutrition to prevent bunch stem necrosis
Scout weekly for downy mildew and powdery mildew during humid weather

severity_guidance.LOW: Isolate affected tree. Scout for Asian Citrus Psyllid (Diaphorina citri) vectors on tender young flushes.
severity_guidance.MEDIUM: Control psyllid vectors immediately: Spray Imidacloprid 17.8 SL @ 0.5ml/L or Thiamethoxam 25 WG @ 0.3g/L.
severity_guidance.HIGH: HLB is incurable. Remove and burn confirmed positive trees to stop spread to orchard. Spray psyllid insecticide before tree removal.

cultural_practices: Plant only certified disease-free, tested budwood stock from registered insect-proof nurseries
Deploy yellow sticky traps (10 per acre) to detect and monitor psyllid populations
Apply foliar micronutrient cocktail (Zinc, Manganese, Iron) to support declining tree vigor
Maintain orchard weed sanitation and remove alternate hosts like Murraya paniculata (orange jasmine)
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).monitoring_note: Check new flush shoots for asymmetric blotchy mottle on leaves and psyllid nymphs.

severity_guidance.LOW: Remove infected shoots. Avoid overhead irrigation and minimize wind-blown dust abrasion.
severity_guidance.MEDIUM: Apply Copper hydroxide @ 1.5g/L or Copper octanoate during dormant and petal fall stages at low rates to avoid phytotoxicity.
severity_guidance.HIGH: Apply Oxytetracycline (Mycoshield) @ 1.5g/L every 7 days during warm rainy periods from shuck split.

cultural_practices: Plant tolerant cultivars (e.g., Candor, Dixired, Redhaven) and avoid highly susceptible varieties
Plant windbreaks around the orchard perimeter to prevent blowing sand abrasive injury
Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilization which prolongs succulent vegetative growth
Peach___Bacterial_spot.monitoring_note: Inspect young leaves for small angular water-soaked spots that drop out creating 'shot-hole' effect.

severity_guidance.LOW: Leaves are broad, lustrous green, and free of leaf curl, shot-hole, or bacterial spots.
severity_guidance.MEDIUM: Vigorous tree. Maintain summer pruning for sunlight penetration to lower fruiting wood.
severity_guidance.HIGH: Optimal tree health. Ensure uniform irrigation during stone hardening and fruit swell.

cultural_practices: Annual pruning to vase shape for optimal interior air and light penetration
Maintain weed-free ring with organic mulch around the trunk drip line
Apply dormant copper-oil spray before bud swell to prevent peach leaf curl

severity_guidance.LOW: Remove and discard lower infected leaves. Disinfect hands and tools before touching healthy plants.
severity_guidance.MEDIUM: Apply Copper Hydroxide 77 WP @ 2g/L combined with Mancozeb 75 WP @ 2g/L every 7 days (copper-mancozeb tank mix overcomes copper resistance).
severity_guidance.HIGH: Apply Kasugamycin 3% SL @ 2ml/L or Streptomycin Sulfate (bactericide) @ 0.5g/L. Avoid handling plants when foliage is damp.

cultural_practices: Use only certified hot-water treated pathogen-free pepper seeds and healthy nursery transplants
Use drip irrigation exclusively — never use overhead sprinklers which spread bacteria
Practice 2-3 year crop rotation away from solanaceous crops (tomato, potato, eggplant)
Clean stakes and trellis wires with 10% bleach solution between crop cycles
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.monitoring_note: Re-scan within 6 days. Inspect new leaves for water-soaked spots turning dark with yellow halos.

severity_guidance.LOW: Foliage is dark green, turgid, and robust with no necrotic lesions or mosaic mottling.
severity_guidance.MEDIUM: Vigorous stand. Maintain regular calcium feeding to prevent blossom end rot in developing peppers.
severity_guidance.HIGH: Excellent crop condition. Continue regular scouting for thrips, mites, and aphids.

cultural_practices: Maintain uniform soil moisture using plastic mulch and drip fertigation
Apply calcium nitrate fertigation during active fruit set to prevent calcium deficiency
Stake plants to keep branches and developing fruit off wet soil

severity_guidance.LOW: Targeted spot removal on bottom leaves. Improve potassium fertilization to boost plant vigor.
severity_guidance.MEDIUM: Apply Mancozeb 75 WP @ 2.5g/L or Chlorothalonil 75 WP @ 2g/L every 7-10 days.
severity_guidance.HIGH: Apply systemic curative fungicide: Azoxystrobin + Difenoconazole @ 1ml/L or Pyraclostrobin @ 1ml/L. Ensure thorough under-leaf coverage.

cultural_practices: Plant certified, disease-free seed tubers with balanced fertilization (avoid nitrogen deficit)
Hill soil adequately around stems to protect tubers from spore wash-down
Schedule irrigation in early morning so foliage dries rapidly under sunlight
Rotate fields on a 3-year cycle with non-host crops like cereals or legumes
Potato___Early_blight.monitoring_note: Check concentric 'target board' rings in brown spots on middle and lower leaves.

severity_guidance.LOW: Preventive action: Spray Mancozeb 75 WP @ 2.5g/L or Chlorothalonil @ 2g/L immediately upon cool, humid weather forecast.
severity_guidance.MEDIUM: Apply Cymoxanil 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP @ 2.5g/L or Dimethomorph 50 WP @ 1g/L. Destroy infected plant foci.
severity_guidance.HIGH: EMERGENCY: Apply Metalaxyl 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP @ 2.5g/L or Infinito (Fluopicolide + Propamocarb) @ 1.5ml/L immediately. If widespread near harvest, destroy haulms with Reglone.

cultural_practices: Plant strictly certified disease-free seed tubers; cull out soft or rot-affected tubers before planting
Destroy all volunteer potatoes and cull piles before the season starts — primary infection source
Maintain high soil ridges (earthing up) to create at least 10 cm barrier preventing tuber infection
Do not harvest when vines are wet or green; kill haulms 10-14 days prior to digging tubers
Potato___Late_blight.monitoring_note: CRITICAL: Re-scan within 4 days. Look for water-soaked lesions with white mold on leaf undersides.

severity_guidance.LOW: Dense, healthy canopy without leaf lesions, wilting, or yellowing. Tuber initiation proceeding well.
severity_guidance.MEDIUM: Vigorous crop. Maintain regular earthing up and preventive protective fungicide sprays during cloudy weather.
severity_guidance.HIGH: Optimal health. Continue balanced potash fertigation to support tuber bulk.

cultural_practices: Maintain thorough earthing up to prevent greening and blight spore exposure to tubers
Avoid waterlogging in furrows; ensure rapid field drainage
Scout for aphid vectors of Potato Virus Y (PVY)

severity_guidance.LOW: Canes and foliage are strong, green, and upright without cane blight, spur blight, or rust signs.
severity_guidance.MEDIUM: Healthy canes. Ensure proper trellis support and wire training.
severity_guidance.HIGH: Excellent condition. Maintain regular organic mulch and drip watering.

cultural_practices: Prune out spent floricanes right down to the ground immediately after harvest
Thin primocanes to 4-5 vigorous canes per foot of row to ensure air circulation
Irrigate at ground level with drip lines to keep berries and foliage dry

severity_guidance.LOW: Trifoliate leaves are clean, vibrant green, and nodulation is healthy on root systems.
severity_guidance.MEDIUM: Vigorous crop canopy. Monitor for pod borers and rust during flowering and pod development.
severity_guidance.HIGH: Optimal crop health. Maintain adequate soil moisture during R3-R5 reproductive stages.

cultural_practices: Ensure seed inoculation with Rhizobium japonicum before sowing for nitrogen fixation
Maintain weed-free field conditions during initial 35 days
Scout regularly for defoliators (Spodoptera litura) and Asian soybean rust

severity_guidance.LOW: Remove first infected older leaves with white talcum-like spots. Increase plant spacing.
severity_guidance.MEDIUM: Apply Potassium Bicarbonate @ 4g/L or Wettable Sulfur 80 WP @ 2.5g/L or Neem Oil 0.5% early in the morning.
severity_guidance.HIGH: Apply systemic fungicide: Myclobutanil 10 WP @ 0.5g/L or Trifloxystrobin @ 0.5g/L. Repeat in 7-10 days.

cultural_practices: Plant powdery mildew-tolerant or resistant squash hybrids (e.g., PMR cultivars)
Provide wide row spacing (minimum 1.5 - 2 meters between rows) for maximum airflow and sun exposure
Avoid overhead irrigation; use drip irrigation underneath mulch
Remove and destroy all crop residues immediately after final harvest
Squash___Powdery_mildew.monitoring_note: Re-scan upper and lower leaf surfaces for expanding white powder colonies.

severity_guidance.LOW: Remove purple-bordered spotted leaves during runner training. Clear old dead foliage.
severity_guidance.MEDIUM: Apply Captan 50 WP @ 2g/L or Copper Hydroxide @ 1.5g/L before flowering and after renovation.
severity_guidance.HIGH: Apply Pyraclostrobin + Boscalid (Pristine) @ 1g/L or Thiophanate-methyl 70 WP @ 1g/L. Repeat in 10 days.

cultural_practices: Plant certified virus- and pathogen-free runner plants on raised beds with drip irrigation
Mow and renovate strawberry beds after harvest, discarding infected foliage debris
Avoid excessive nitrogen applications in spring which encourage dense foliage and humidity
Maintain 25-30 cm plant spacing so leaves dry rapidly each morning
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.monitoring_note: Inspect leaves for irregular purplish blotches turning brown and scorched around margins.

severity_guidance.LOW: Crowns and leaves are vigorous, rich green, and productive with healthy white blossom development.
severity_guidance.MEDIUM: Vigorous crop. Maintain clean black plastic or straw mulch beneath berry clusters.
severity_guidance.HIGH: Optimal plant health. Ensure steady boron and potassium fertigation during fruiting.

cultural_practices: Keep developing fruit elevated on straw or mulch away from wet soil to prevent leather rot
Pick ripe fruit promptly and discard any overripe or damaged berries
Scout for two-spotted spider mites on leaf undersides

severity_guidance.LOW: Remove lower infected leaves showing greasy water-soaked specks. Sanitize tools in 70% alcohol.
severity_guidance.MEDIUM: Apply Copper Hydroxide 77 WP @ 2g/L tank-mixed with Mancozeb 75 WP @ 2g/L every 7 days (the combination synergizes bactericidal copper activity).
severity_guidance.HIGH: Apply Kasugamycin 3% SL @ 2ml/L or Streptomycin Sulfate @ 0.5g/L. Remove severely diseased plants to save remainder of field.

cultural_practices: Always use certified pathogen-free seeds (hot water treated at 50°C for 25 minutes)
Never work in tomato fields when leaves are wet from dew or rainfall
Use drip irrigation; avoid overhead watering that splashes bacteria between plants
Rotate crops on a 2-3 year cycle avoiding tomato, potato, pepper, and eggplant
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.monitoring_note: Inspect young leaves and fruit calyx for small water-soaked dark spots with yellow halos.

severity_guidance.LOW: Prune off lower 30 cm of leaves touching soil. Apply organic mulch around plant base.
severity_guidance.MEDIUM: Apply Mancozeb 75 WP @ 2.5g/L or Chlorothalonil 75 WP @ 2g/L every 7-10 days.
severity_guidance.HIGH: Apply Azoxystrobin 18.2% + Difenoconazole 11.4% SC @ 1ml/L or Pyraclostrobin @ 1ml/L. Spray thoroughly to leaf undersides.

cultural_practices: Stake and prune indeterminate tomatoes to maintain strong upright habit and air circulation
Mulch with straw or black plastic film to prevent soil-dwelling spores splashing onto lower leaves
Water at base using drip irrigation; keep foliage dry
Destroy and remove crop residues after harvest; never compost blighted foliage
Tomato___Early_blight.monitoring_note: Check concentric target-like rings in brown spots on lower leaves for signs of active spore growth.

severity_guidance.LOW: Preventive protection: Spray Mancozeb 75 WP @ 2.5g/L or Chlorothalonil 75 WP @ 2g/L immediately when humid, overcast weather is forecast.
severity_guidance.MEDIUM: Apply Dimethomorph 50 WP @ 1g/L or Cymoxanil 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP @ 2.5g/L. Repeat every 5-7 days under wet conditions.
severity_guidance.HIGH: EMERGENCY: Apply Metalaxyl 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP @ 2.5g/L or Fluopicolide + Propamocarb (Infinito) @ 1.5ml/L immediately. Rogue out and burn heavily infected plants.

cultural_practices: Avoid planting tomatoes near potato fields (both are major hosts for late blight epidemics)
Ensure maximum plant spacing (60 cm in row, 90 cm between rows) for quick canopy drying
Eliminate volunteer tomato and potato plants in and around fields before planting
Drip irrigate early in the morning so sun evaporates any accidental leaf wetness
Tomato___Late_blight.monitoring_note: CRITICAL: Re-scan within 4 days. Monitor for rapidly enlarging water-soaked greasy gray-green blotches with white fungal fuzz.

severity_guidance.LOW: Increase greenhouse ventilation immediately. Lower relative humidity below 85%. Prune bottom foliage.
severity_guidance.MEDIUM: Apply Copper Oxychloride 50 WP @ 3g/L or Chlorothalonil 75 WP @ 2g/L. Spray underside of leaves thoroughly.
severity_guidance.HIGH: Apply Difenoconazole 25 EC @ 0.5ml/L or Tebuconazole 250 EC @ 1ml/L. Increase heated ventilation if in polyhouse.

cultural_practices: Maintain active greenhouse ventilation and circulation fans to prevent still, humid air pockets
Keep temperatures slightly warmer at night to reduce relative humidity
Prune lower suckers and dense leaves to allow light and air through plant middle
Use resistant varieties carrying Cf resistance genes (e.g. Cf-9, Cf-11)
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.monitoring_note: Inspect leaf undersides for velvety olive-green to brown fungal growth directly below pale yellow upper patches.

severity_guidance.LOW: Remove infected lower leaves promptly. Mulch bare soil around root zone.
severity_guidance.MEDIUM: Apply Mancozeb 75 WP @ 2.5g/L or Chlorothalonil 75 WP @ 2g/L every 7 days during warm, rainy weather.
severity_guidance.HIGH: Apply Azoxystrobin 23 SC @ 1ml/L or Copper Hydroxide @ 2g/L tank-mixed with Mancozeb @ 2g/L. Prune infected stems.

cultural_practices: Mulch heavily around tomato base to prevent rain splash of fungal spores from soil
Stake plants vertically and remove suckers up to first fruit cluster
Practice 3-year crop rotation without solanaceous crops
Do not work in wet tomato rows to avoid mechanically transferring spores on clothing and tools
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.monitoring_note: Check for small circular spots (2-3mm) with gray centers and tiny black pycnidia speckles.

severity_guidance.LOW: Apply strong water jet to undersides of leaves to knock down mite colonies. Spray Neem Oil 0.5% solution.
severity_guidance.MEDIUM: Apply Spiromesifen 22.9 SC @ 1ml/L or Propargite 57 EC @ 2ml/L. Release predatory mites (Phytoseiulus persimilis).
severity_guidance.HIGH: Apply Abamectin 1.8 EC @ 0.5ml/L or Fenpyroximate 5 EC @ 1ml/L. Wet leaf undersides completely where webbing is dense.

cultural_practices: Avoid water stress — spider mites thrive and reproduce exponentially under hot, dry, dusty conditions
Wash perimeter dirt roads with water or establish windbreak vegetation to reduce dust buildup on leaves
Avoid broad-spectrum synthetic pyrethroids which kill beneficial predatory mites and cause mite resurgence
Destroy heavily infested plants at end of season to avoid overwintering
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.monitoring_note: Examine leaf undersides with a hand lens for tiny moving mites, yellow stippling, and fine silken webs.

severity_guidance.LOW: Prune out diseased leaves from lower canopy. Ensure plants are staked and trellised.
severity_guidance.MEDIUM: Apply Chlorothalonil 75 WP @ 2g/L or Mancozeb 75 WP @ 2.5g/L at first sign of lesions.
severity_guidance.HIGH: Apply Azoxystrobin 23 SC @ 1ml/L or Fluxapyroxad + Pyraclostrobin @ 0.8ml/L. Reapply every 7-10 days.

cultural_practices: Maintain generous plant spacing for rapid air drying throughout the canopy
Eliminate solanaceous weeds and volunteer crops that harbor Corynespora fungus
Apply balanced nitrogen; avoid excessive vegetative canopy shading
Remove all plant debris and deep-plow after harvest
Tomato___Target_Spot.monitoring_note: Check for brown circular lesions with concentric rings and faint yellow halos on leaves, stems, and green fruit.

severity_guidance.LOW: Virus has no chemical cure. Immediately rogue out and bag infected plants displaying upward leaf cupping and stunting.
severity_guidance.MEDIUM: Control vector Whitefly (Bemisia tabaci): Spray Imidacloprid 17.8 SL @ 0.5ml/L or Thiamethoxam 25 WG @ 0.3g/L or Spirotetramat @ 1ml/L.
severity_guidance.HIGH: Deploy silver reflective mulch to repel whiteflies. Spray Acetamiprid 20 SP @ 0.5g/L. Rogue out all symptomatic plants immediately.

cultural_practices: Plant certified TYLCV-resistant hybrids (e.g. Ty-1, Ty-2, Ty-3 gene varieties like US-440, Abhinav)
Use 40-50 mesh insect-proof netting in seedling nursery tunnels to produce 100% virus-free transplants
Deploy yellow sticky traps (15-20 traps per acre) at canopy height to monitor and capture adult whiteflies
Maintain a host-free fallow period or non-host barrier between tomato cycles
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.monitoring_note: Inspect apical growing tips for yellowing, reduction in leaf size, and upward cup-shaped curled leaflets.

severity_guidance.LOW: Virus is incurable and mechanically transmitted. Rogue out and burn infected plants. Wash hands with 20% skim milk or soap.
severity_guidance.MEDIUM: Disinfect all stakes, pruning knives, and trellis clips with 10% trisodium phosphate (TSP) or household bleach.
severity_guidance.HIGH: Isolate the row. Instruct workers not to touch healthy plants after handling infected areas. Control chewing and sap-sucking pests.

cultural_practices: Plant certified mosaic-resistant tomato varieties (designated with 'Tm-2' or 'ToMV' resistance)
Soak seeds in 10% trisodium phosphate (TSP) for 30 minutes before sowing if using farm-saved seed
Prohibit tobacco use near tomatoes — workers smoking or using tobacco must wash hands thoroughly before touching crops
Rotate fields out of tomatoes and peppers for 2 years
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.monitoring_note: Look for light and dark green mosaic patterns on leaves, fern-leaf distortion, and internal brown fruit browning.

severity_guidance.LOW: Vigorous, dark green foliage with healthy blossoms and balanced fruit set. Zero symptoms of blight or virus.
severity_guidance.MEDIUM: Optimal crop health. Continue preventive bio-fungicide (Trichoderma / Bacillus subtilis) root drench.
severity_guidance.HIGH: Excellent condition. Maintain balanced NPK + calcium nitrate fertigation to prevent blossom end rot.

cultural_practices: Ensure uniform soil moisture to avoid fruit cracking and blossom-end calcium disorders
Maintain weekly trellis tying and sucker pruning on indeterminate varieties
Scout foliage weekly for early signs of leaf miner, pinworm, or blight

severity_guidance.LOW: Isolate affected plant area. Remove and safely dispose of spotted or symptomatic leaves. Improve air movement and sunshine exposure.
severity_guidance.MEDIUM: Apply protective broad-spectrum bio-fungicide or copper-based spray (Copper Oxychloride @ 2.5g/L or Mancozeb @ 2g/L). Consult your local Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK).
severity_guidance.HIGH: Consult your local Agricultural Extension Officer or block agriculture department for targeted systemic pesticide recommendations.

cultural_practices: Remove and destroy severely affected plant material (do not compost diseased parts)
Water at root level using drip irrigation; keep foliage dry
Improve spacing and trellis support for maximum airflow
Rotate crops away from the host plant family for at least 2 consecutive seasons
Maintain clean agricultural tools disinfected with 70% alcohol or 10% bleach
default_treatment.monitoring_note: Re-scan the affected plants after 7 days to evaluate if symptoms have halted or progressed.
